tip: The -meli suffix means should or must: güvenmelisin = you should believe in yourself. It attaches straight onto the verb stem.
The -la ending means with: arkadaşlarımla = with my friends. It stacks after the possessive: arkadaş, lar, ım, la.
Aorist plus -di means used to: dinlerdi = he used to listen. It marks a repeated past habit, not one finished action.
The -den ending marks a source: benden = from me. Learning from someone uses it, so öğrenmek pairs with the -den form.
The -ama inside a verb means cannot: alışamadım = I couldn't get used to it. Without it, alışmadım = I didn't get used to it.
After a number the noun stays singular: iki kedi, not kediler, and bir köpek stays bare. The number already signals plural.
Negative future is stem plus -ma plus future -acak: çıkmayacağız = we will not go out, from çık, ma, yacağız.
The verb çıkmak takes the -e form for a goal: yürüyüşe çıkarım = I go out for a walk. The walk carries the dative -e.
The -miş ending marks news you infer or were told, not saw: kalmış = it apparently stayed closed.
The -an ending builds a who does clause: mısır satan amca = the uncle who sells corn. satan describes amca.
Possession pairs two endings: the owner gets -ın, the thing gets -sı, giving babamın arabası = my father's car.
Proper names take an apostrophe before a case ending: Ankara'da = in Ankara. Common nouns skip it, like hastanede.
The -diği ending builds a past relative clause on an object: kaybettiği anahtar = the key that he lost.
The -ce ending turns an adjective into a manner adverb: sessizce = quietly, from sessiz = quiet.
